findings.where: Screen 13, Keep this card, The rule, first line
findings.what: The summary rule's line "A = L1 + L2   B = L2 + L3   C = L1 + L3" loses its spaces when drawn and reads as one garbled equation, "A = L1 + L2 B = L2 + L3 C = L1 + L3", at both 360 and 1280 px, and it wraps "C = L1 + / L3" on a phone; put each loop on its own line or separate them with commas.

findings.where: Screen 13, Keep this card, The rule
findings.what: "R_t" shows as a literal underscore because the card does not subscript it the way screen 7 does, and at 360 px the R20 and Check lines break mid-bracket; write "Rt" or "R at t °C", and keep each formula short enough not to wrap.

findings.where: Screen 13, Keep this card, String B figures (case figure 2c)
findings.what: L2's deviation shows as "0.41%" with no sign, yet the lesson calls it 0.41% high and treats −0.41% as a slip; make the case figure's text "+0.41%" so the card keeps the direction.

Only the P leads are swapped "so the meter can sit further back", but the 5 m C leads still hold the meter at the cable end; swap both sets for 30 m leads, which keeps "It stays at 339.31 mΩ" right, and give the third choice a new slip.

findings.where: Screen 2, Phase ID, the assumed order
findings.what: The order says each core is tested to the screen "from both ends", but the steps only test from your end and never say the ends then swap, as the case file's assumption does; add "Then the two ends swap jobs and repeat."

findings.where: Screen 6, worked example, the note under the lines
findings.what: "Call the results L1, L2 and L3. A, B and C are the loops." has nothing on screen to answer, because no result is labelled A, B or C there; write "Name each result by its core, never by a loop letter." or drop the line.
"38.115 mΩ is L2's formula" calls a number a formula; write "38.115 mΩ comes from L2's formula, and 38.45 mΩ is half of loop A."

findings.where: Screen 1 wrong-answer feedback and screen 8 slip hint
findings.what: "Add the two loops that hold L1, A and C, then take away B" reads at first as a list of L1, A and C; write "Add A and C, the two loops that hold L1, then take away B", and the same for L2 on screen 8.

findings.where: Screen 3, The why, the line under the readouts
findings.what: "8.84% is far more than the 2% a core is allowed" shows from the first, two-wire state, before he has seen 8.84%; show it only on "P on the C clamps", or start it "P on the clamps still reads 8.84% high".

findings.where: Screen 3, The why, second and third paragraphs
findings.what: "The voltage it sees ÷ the current it sends" puts a division sign in a sentence, and "The P leads are measured" is unclear; write "divided by" and "The meter measures the voltage on the P leads".
The question asks "Is it acceptable?" but he can only type the percentage, and the feedback answers it for him; drop the second question, or add a short pass or fail choice after the number.

findings.where: Screen 8 readings and the practice text's DLRO range rule
findings.what: The loops are given to 0.01 mΩ, but the practice text puts a 340 mΩ loop on the DLRO10HD's 1 A range, which its cited data sheet resolves to 0.1 mΩ; add one plain line that the practice readings keep 0.01 mΩ for the working.

The far-end link and its contacts sit between the P points in every loop, so four wires at the OSS do not remove them, and each core takes half the link; one short sentence saying so follows from the screen 3 rule and would change how he fits the link.

The brief promised a state that solves three loops for three cores as he types them, but the picture only steps through which cores each loop holds and never shows a number; the worked example and Section A cover the sums, so this gap is small.

The SVG labels draw at about 11 px on a 360 px phone, and L3's "open" sits about 2 px above the legend row, so the two read as one block; move the legend down a few units and enlarge the labels slightly.

findings.where: Screen 11, Section B b1 points 4 and 5
findings.what: Points 4 and 5 both credit "only what lies between the P points counts", so one idea can earn two of the three points needed; merge them, or make point 5 only about the C clamps' contacts staying outside the measured stretch.
"So a two-wire reading is no good" is absolute where the lesson itself shows a reading 26.52% high; write "So a two-wire reading can be well out."
